description: Baseline: readability+markdown extraction. 3/3 success. Case1=7, Case2=3, Case3=13 steps.

asi.bottleneck: case3 admin-count-shops took 13 steps - likely struggling to navigate to shops list
asi.case2_note: example.com took 3 steps which seems high for simple extraction - could be 1-2

description: Prompt: added rules 10-11 (read DOM carefully, admin nav links). Increased DOM snapshot to 3000/4000 chars, markdown truncation to 4000. 23→16 steps, Case3: 13→4.

asi.hypothesis: Larger DOM + prompt guidance to read DOM before extracting reduces unnecessary steps
asi.key_win: Case3 admin-count-shops 13→4 steps - agent now reads shop count directly from DOM instead of scrolling around
asi.case1_regression: Case1 went 7→9 steps, may need attention

description: Added markdown mode for selector-based extracts, expanded readability positive patterns + form/table candidates. 16→20 steps, regression.

asi.hypothesis: selector-based markdown + admin-friendly readability scoring would help
asi.rollback_reason: 16→20 steps, Case1 regressed 9→12 and Case3 regressed 4→6 despite Case2 improving 3→2
asi.next_action_hint: LLM nondeterminism is high - focus on structural changes that reduce the number of tool calls needed, not tweaks to extraction quality

description: DOM snapshot: show 5 table rows (was 3), add page-info counts (paginator/results). 16→14 steps.

asi.hypothesis: More table rows and page-level count info in DOM helps agent answer without extra navigation
asi.key_insight: Showing more table data and paginator info lets agent read counts directly from DOM

description: Added rule 12 (combine login+nav), increased MAX_ELEMENTS to 60. Regressed to 23 steps — LLM nondeterminism.

asi.hypothesis: More prompt rules + more elements would help
asi.rollback_reason: 14→23 regression, extra prompt verbosity may have confused the model
asi.next_action_hint: User wants to try passing ALL page content (links, buttons, actionable items) to LLM upfront so it can decide in one shot without scrolling

description: Full page action map: replace DOM snapshot with complete page map (all links/buttons/fields regardless of visibility). Prompt updated to tell agent DOM is complete. Case1: 8→6, Case3: 4→3. Case2: 2→5 regressed but overall tied at 14.

asi.hypothesis: Full page map eliminates need to scroll, agent can act directly on all elements
asi.concern: Case2 example.com 2→5 regressed, bigger DOM may overwhelm for simple pages
asi.next_action_hint: Try reducing page_map verbosity for simple pages or adding heuristic to use dom_snapshot for small pages

description: Confirmation run of page map changes. 14→11 steps. Case1=6, Case2=2, Case3=3. Previous Case2=5 was LLM variance.

asi.hypothesis: Stability check of page map approach
asi.key_insight: Page map is stable - Case2 variance (2 vs 5) confirms LLM nondeterminism, not a real regression

description: New baseline with 3 complex admin cases: shop-hours(6), agent-details(4), count-shops(3). All pass. 13 total steps.
Capped nav to 20 links + increased field value to 150 chars. Same 13 steps, but nav cap is Django-overfitting.

asi.hypothesis: Trim nav sidebar, increase field value display
asi.rollback_reason: Nav cap at 20 is overfitting to Django admin - other dashboards may have essential nav links beyond 20
asi.next_action_hint: Instead of hard-capping nav, try smarter deduplication (remove Add/Change pairs that repeat) or a general char budget that naturally prioritizes content over nav
